blocks.content: Article 170 of the Constitution provides for the composition of the Legislative Assemblies of each State.

rows: Permanent body (1/3rd members retire every 2 years)
Exclusive power to introduce and pass

items: State assemblies with fewer than 60 seats (Sikkim, Mizoram, Goa, and Puducherry) are frequently tested exception cases.
Money Bills originate solely in the Vidhan Sabha; the Vidhan Parishad can only delay a Money Bill for up to 14 days.
The minimum age qualification for election to the Vidhan Sabha is 25 years.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Legislative Assembly (Vidhan Sabha) is the directly elected lower house of the state legislature in India.
Article 170 specifies that the maximum strength of a Legislative Assembly is 500 and the minimum strength is 60.
Exceptions to the minimum strength requirement include Sikkim (32), Mizoram (40), Goa (40), and Puducherry (30).
The normal term of the Legislative Assembly is 5 years, but it can be dissolved earlier by the Governor.
Money Bills can only be introduced in the Legislative Assembly and cannot be introduced in the Legislative Council.
